header: TERM FAMILIES: words that people at the plant use for the same thing, though their dictionary meanings differ. My words, 23 Nov 2026: "In DSP, Biometric, face recognition, RFID and BAMS are all used interchangeably for the same purpose, though they are not the same in literal meaning. Take them as logically equal, along with their individual literal meaning. Keep both sides, to handle any unforeseen query: who will refer to what, we do not know." So a question that uses ONE word of a family is searched for ALL of them, and nothing is taken away: the typed words stay (their own literal meaning still counts), the others are ADDED. I built it as a general capability, not a rule for one question:
- the question's embedding is made from the question plus the family's other words (src/lib/ai/geminiEmbedding.ts, for every kind of search at once);
- the circulars' and announcements' word search (a Postgres text-search OR query) gets the other words as extra alternatives (semanticPolicySearch.ts, announcementSemanticSearch.ts);
- the per-word rescue of the content search (semanticContentSearch.ts) gets them too.

I leave the test that counts how many of the TYPED words a passage holds (isLexicalHit) alone: the added words widen what is FOUND, they never make a passage look like a worse match for what was typed. To add a new family, add one entry in FAMILIES. This file is pure (no server code, no database).

behaviours: a word of the family brings the other three
face recognition (also facial recognition, face-recognition) brings the others
RFID and BAMS each bring the others, in any case
a question that already uses several only gets the missing ones
a question with no family word is not touched
part of another word is not a family word (bamsa, rfidx, biometricx are not)
the typed words stay in the embedding text: both sides are kept
the text-search pieces are valid tsquery fragments (words, or a phrase joined by <->)
every term of every family finds itself (the pattern matches its own text)
no word belongs to two families (a word's family must be one)
the embedding of every search question is made from the question and its family words
the circulars' word search adds the family words
the announcements' word search adds the family words, and the coverage test of the typed words is untouched
the content search's per-word rescue adds them
